messages:
Ashley Support: FYI customer ACME says their SIEM hasn't received audit events for a subset of accounts since yesterday evening. They noticed missing 'policy.change' and some 'create_key' events. Ticket #INC-4728
Maria SecOps: Can you paste the job id + export manifest? Are they using the Splunk HEC forwarder or S3 delivery? @Tom SRE please eyeball.
Ashley Support: Forwarder type: splunk-hec via our audit-forwarder lambda. Job id: export-2026-03-16-21-34. Manifest: s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/2026/03/16/export-2026-03-16-21-34/manifest.json
Tom SRE: seeing repeated 403s in the forwarder logs starting at 21:38 UTC. snippet from CloudWatch:
```
ERROR Request failed: status=403, body={"message":"The request signature we calculated does not match the signature you provided."}
```
Tom SRE: That usually points to KMS/CMK mismatch or key rotation. Any KMS alias rotations happened last night? @Leo Security Bot do we have KMS rotation events?
Leo Security Bot: automated alert: CMK alias/rotation for alias/redwood-audit-cmk created at 2026-03-16T21:30:22Z (key id: 1234abcd-rot). Previous key id: 7890efgh-prev. Rotation was performed as part of scheduled rotation window.
Maria SecOps: aha. forwarder uses decrypt permission for the key id it was originally configured with (7890efgh-prev). Since alias now points to 1234abcd-rot, the forwarder role's key policy needs to include the new key id OR forwarder must use alias (kms:ViaService) — looks like the forwarder was pinned to the key ARN with the old key id.
Ashley Support: customer attached a sample missing-event JSON from their SIEM. It's in the export bucket but the forwarder failed before sending; so events exist in S3. They want immediate replay.
Tom SRE: short repro for ops: run aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports/prod/2026/.../export-2026-03-16-21-34/batch-0001.ndjson - | head
Also check forwarder logs:
```
/aws/lambda/audit-forwarder-prod ERROR decrypt failed KeyId=7890efgh-prev
```
Maria SecOps: mitigation options:
1) Re-encrypt objects in bucket with the new CMK id and run replay job.
2) Add decrypt permission for forwarder role on the new key (quickest) — but need compliance signoff because it modifies key policy.
3) Temporarily point alias back to old key (not ideal for security but fastest if approved).
Tom SRE: I'll kick off an emergency replay once permissions fixed. I'll also add a small check to the forwarder to prefer alias usage instead of pinned KeyId.
Ashley Support: customer wants ETA. Can we give 2-4 hours? Also they asked if retention/field-stripping might be involved — they provided an example where actor.email is missing from some entries.
Maria SecOps: actor.email missing is likely a pre-export filter in our pipeline (older tenants had PII redaction toggle). Confirmed: tenant acme-corp had PII_FILTER=1 in their tenant config at time of export. That explains missing email fields — separate from forwarder failure.
Ashley Support: noted. I told them: events present in S3 but delivery failed due to KMS key rotation; some PII intentionally redacted for their tenant. They asked for a full replay and confirmation of schema completeness.
Tom SRE: Action items:
- Maria to request KMS compliance approval to add decrypt for forwarder role to new key (or provide signed authorization to temporarily repoint alias) (ASSIGNED: Maria)
- Tom to run replay job after permissions (ASSIGNED: Tom)
- I will patch forwarder to use alias going forward and add alert for KeyId mismatch (PR planned) (ASSIGNED: Tom)
- Ashley to update customer with ETA and note PII redaction behavior (ASSIGNED: Ashley)
Maria SecOps: filing a short SOC change request, ETA 90m for approval. Adding audit trail.
Deploy-Bot: deploy queued: audit-forwarder patch -> branch/fix/kms-alias-usage, CI passed.
Tom SRE: thanks all. ping me if ACME needs an expedited replay; I'll do manual replay now if we get permissions.
Ashley Support: thanks — updating ticket and emailing customer. :thumbsup:
